I've saved the Q3 answers to `answer.json`. Using the same method on Q2 gives all 10 reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 355,664,172 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | svc, 356,622,164 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u188@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 235 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 660,762 |
| h. August → September growth | -5.8% |

The definitions alone didn't reproduce the reference values. Three things had to be inferred from the data:
- **Dates are in Korean time (UTC+9).** Order times are stored in UTC. Using them as-is gave Q2 numbers that didn't match the reference.
- **Customers are identified by email.** Emails are compared ignoring case and surrounding spaces. There are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails, so b and f would come out too high otherwise.
- **Segment and category names were cleaned up.** The same value appears with different capitalisation and stray spaces (e.g. "smb" and "SMB"), so these were normalised before grouping.

STATUS: DONE
